name: Tallow skincare

lead: Tallow skincare means using rendered beef fat, alone or blended into balms, as a face and body moisturiser. It spread through ancestral-diet and wellness communities as part of a move toward traditional, minimally processed fats, and users choose it over conventional creams.

The chain is that fats and oils on skin generally act as occlusives, forming a layer that slows water loss, which leaves skin softer and less dry-looking. Proponents say tallow's fatty acid profile resembles human skin oils. No published trial was found testing tallow on skin.

paras: People rub a small amount of whipped tallow balm onto the face, often after cleansing or at night, and some blend it with other oils. Users report on how skin feels within days to weeks.

There are no published safety studies for tallow as a skin product. Moisturisers in general can cause contact dermatitis in some users, and animal fats can go rancid or carry contaminants depending on preparation.

studies.title: Beef Tallow-Based Skincare Claims in Social Media: A Cross-Sectional Analysis.

angle.text: Users apply whipped tallow balm to the face as a moisturiser, preferring a simple animal-fat product to conventional creams. Fats on skin slow water loss, which is the route to softer skin; published trials on tallow itself are lacking.

lead: Tallow skincare is the practice of applying rendered beef fat to the skin as a moisturiser, often in the form of a whipped balm. It is an application of beef tallow, a fat historically used in soap and candles [1].

Proponents online say tallow is a traditional, minimally processed moisturiser whose fatty acid profile resembles human skin oils. Moisturisers in general are described as products that protect and lubricate skin, largely by forming an occlusive layer that slows water loss [2].
No published human trial was found testing tallow on skin, and Wikipedia's articles on tallow and emollients do not discuss its skincare use [1][2].
infobox: Sold as cosmetics or homemade; not evaluated as a drug

paras: Tallow is rendered beef, pork or mutton fat made mostly of triglycerides. Beef tallow is about 50 percent saturated, 42 percent monounsaturated and 4 percent polyunsaturated fat, and its main fatty acids are palmitic, stearic and oleic acids [1]. Industrial tallow is the main raw material for soap [1].

Water constantly evaporates from skin, and moisturisers slow this loss as occlusives, which form a water-repelling film, or as humectants, which attract water. Petrolatum is reported to reduce water loss by about 50 to 75 percent for several hours [2]. Common ingredients include shea butter, lanolin and plant oils [2]. Daily moisturiser use can help comfort in eczema, and persistent use of products containing allergens or irritants can cause contact dermatitis [2]. Wikipedia's emollient article does not discuss tallow or animal fats in general [2].

Tallow balm is discussed in ancestral-diet and wellness circles as a natural alternative to commercial moisturisers. Proponents claim it suits skin because of its fatty acid composition. These claims have not been tested in published studies.
No studies found. No published human trial was found testing beef tallow applied to skin.
